residue_classification.cause: a changed body may also contain pre-existing `((T*)((byte*)E + N))[0]` lines emitted by the _wide_raw_lvalue path in BOTH sources; whole-body canonicalization over-strips those, so the residue is a false positive of the hash method, not a second change
residue_classification.check: fresh-process line-pair comparison, one process per source

conclusion: all changed bodies differ from the main source only by the fix-124 byte wrapper
method: tier 1: re-lift each changed row from the branch source, delete every fix-124 byte wrapper, and require an exact hash match against the main-source manifest; tier 2: for the rows where that hash method over-strips, compare both sources' fresh bodies line by line and require every differing pair to be a wrapper-added pair
